publish_job.theorem_title: Exact finite count from projection survival
publish_job.formal_statement:
theorem paley_projection_survival_count {α β : Type*} (S : Finset α) (P : Finset β)
    (R : α → β → Prop) [∀ a b, Decidable (R a b)]
    (q t K : ℕ) (hq : 2 ≤ q) (ht : 1 ≤ t) (hK : K < q)
    (hP : P.card + 1 = q * t)
    (hS : ∀ a ∈ S, (q - 1) * t ≤ (P.bipartiteAbove R a).card)
    (hcap : ∀ b ∈ P, (S.bipartiteBelow R b).card ≤ K) :
    S.card ≤ K := by sorry
publish_job.natural_language_statement:
Let $S$ and $P$ be finite sets and let $R\subseteq S\times P$ be a relation. Suppose $q,t,K$ are natural numbers with $q\ge2$, $t\ge1$, and $K<q$. Assume $|P|+1=qt$, every element of $S$ is related to at least $(q-1)t$ elements of $P$, and every element of $P$ is related to at most $K$ elements of $S$. Then

$$|S|\le K.$$

The assertion includes empty $S$, $K=0$, $t=1$, and $K=q-1$. It supplies the exact integer-count step in nonzero projection arguments. The incidence hypotheses are explicit; finite-field projection counts and code-theoretic witnesses are not part of this statement.
